newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Saudi Arabia worried by any threat to Iraq's unity.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia worried by any threat to Iraq's unity.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said on Tuesday Iraq must comply with all Gulf war Security Council resolutions but expressed concern over any threat to its unity and territorial integrity.

In a speech to the General Assembly, Saudi Arabia's Assistant Foreign Minister Abdul-Rahman Mansouri backed the "honorable and firm stand taken by the international community following the brutal Iraqi aggression" against Kuwait in 1990.

He said Saudi Arabia's position was based on two principles. One was ensuring Iraq's comprehensive and total compliance with all Security Council resolutions. The other was commitment to the preservation of the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and alleviation of the suffering of its people.

"However, we are concerned with the possibility that the latest developments in northern Iraq might threaten the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq, since certain neighbouring countriers have attempted to interfere in the conflict in the Kurdish areas under various guises."

This was an allusion to involvement by Iran and Turkey in the region, which Iraqi troops entered in late August for the first time since the Gulf war in support of one of the warring Kurdish factions.

"In light of these realities, we have to be very careful lest the situation lead to an erosion in the international alliance which is responsible for full implementation of all relevant Security Council resolutions," Mansouri said.

The foremost of these, he added, concerned the release and repatriation of all prisoners of war and detainees from Kuwait and other countries, the return of stolen assets, compensation for war losses, and full cooperation with the U.N. Special Commission charged with eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
